text:
Marathon Petroleum stock rose modestly today, continuing a strong rebound from last week's dip. The gain reflects a stabilizing refining environment: US crude is holding around $90 per barrel, refineries are running at 95.2% capacity, and heating oil prices have spiked 59% year-over-year, which boosts demand for refined products heading into winter. The company has recovered nearly $42 per share over the past five trading days as these tailwinds became clearer.

However, broader oil market dynamics pose a headwind going forward. The IEA reported that Russian crude production has rebounded to 8.73 million barrels per day and global oil supplies have shifted back into surplus, which typically puts downward pressure on crude prices and refinery margins. That oversupply trend, visible in the recent two-week decline, may limit how much further the stock can climb despite strong near-term heating demand.
